survived.title: Eufy in-memory map/pose source has NO vacuum identity — a second Eufy robot is served the FIRST robot's map, rooms, pose and render raster
survived.mechanism: Every in-memory read the coordinator performs for the Eufy backend locates its data with `_msr.eufy_inmem_candidates(self._manager.hass, mem_cfg)` — a function whose ONLY inputs are `hass` and `{hass_data_domain: 'robovac_mqtt', mapdata_attrs: [...]}`. It takes no vacuum_entity_id, no serial, no device_id. It returns (map_source_runtime.py:839-858) `('hass_data', 'robovac_mqtt', hass.data['robovac_mqtt'])` FIRST, then each config entry's runtime_data. `eufy_mapdata_obj_from_candidates` (runtime:957-968) then runs `_walk(root, _holds_mapdata)` — a bounded BFS whose predicate (runtime:949-955) is 'any object exposing `_map_data` whose `room_pixels` is bytes' — and returns the FIRST hit. hass.data['robovac_mqtt'] is the WHOLE domain bucket; per this repo's own adapter comment (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:650) it is `{<entry>: {'coordinators': [EufyCleanCoordinator, ...]}}`, a LIST of robots. So with two Eufy robots the BFS deterministically returns coordinators[0] for EVERY vacuum_entity_id. Because the whole-domain bucket is appended BEFORE the per-entry runtime_data roots, even a two-config-entry install is defeated by candidate ordering. Five coordinator entry points inherit this: `_refresh_eufy_map_source` (line 397 -> static rooms + image_size + hazards), `_read_inmem_pose` (line 461 -> robot/dock/trail), `get_live_mapdata_obj` (line 361), `async_get_map_render_data` (line 645 -> the raster the card DRAWS), `async_get_map_data_dict` (line 689 -> the raster `zone_membership`/`current_room_for_pixel` consume). The per-vacuum `_mem_rooms_cache[vacuum_entity_id]` does not help: its `version` is a sha1 of that same wrong raster, so the cache is self-consistently wrong. The storage FALLBACK is correctly per-device (`eufy_store_path` -> `device_identifier_value(hass, vacuum_entity_id, 'robovac_mqtt')` -> the serial in the device registry), which proves per-device identity was the intent — memory-PRIMARY silently overrides the only correct path.
survived.user_impact: Arithmetic, robot #2 (Eufy 'Bella', map 200x260 px @ 5 cm/px) while robot #1 ('Alfred', 240x180 px) is coordinators[0]: the card for Bella renders Alfred's raster and Alfred's room bboxes. survived.title: Sticky last-known-good hold re-serves a frozen current_room/robot_anchor as `present: True`; the `stale` flag it sets has NO consumer, so a docked Roborock reports a phantom room for up to 6 hours
survived.mechanism: `_commit_result` lines 105-134: when a new result is absent and the reason is not in `_MAP_SOURCE_HARD_CLEAR_REASONS`, it re-publishes the previous result as `held = dict(cached_res)` with `stale=True/stale_since/stale_reason` added — but `held['present']` stays True and every moving field (`current_room`, `robot_anchor`, `dock_anchor`, `path`, `robot_heading`) is carried over verbatim, frozen. For Roborock this is the NORMAL docked state, not an edge case: per .claude/notes/reference_map_source_lifecycle.md the parsed MapData lives only in HA memory and is nulled when the vacuum idles/docks, so `roborock_result_from_candidates` emits `no_parsed_map` — deliberately excluded from the hard-clear set (coordinator:50-55) so it ALWAYS holds. The result carries `current_room` because `overlays_from_mapdata` (runtime:665-667) copies `map_data.vacuum_room`. The docstring at lines 87-99 asserts 'the last-good map is kept and flagged `stale` (the card dims/badges it and freezes the pose)'. That is a false claim about the code: grepping the whole frontend for `stale_since`/`stale_reason`/a stale branch under map_state_source returns nothing — `src/state/map.js:910 mapStateSource()` returns the block verbatim and `mapOverlayData()` (map.js:1055) only overlays `_livePose`, which for Roborock is permanently null because the Roborock adapter declares no `live_pose` block (async_get_map_live_pose returns `not_configured`).
survived.user_impact: Every time a Roborock docks, the map_overlays sensor (sensor/map_overlays.py:73-84, which checks only `res.get('present')` and never `stale`) keeps reporting the last room NAME as its state for up to `_STALE_MAP_TTL_SECONDS` = 6 hours. That state is the recorded value — the sensor's stated purpose is 'a clean room-over-time history' for automations/templates and the recorder — so every dock injects a 6-hour phantom occupancy of the last-cleaned room into the history. Automations templated on the room sensor fire against a room the robot left hours ago. On the card the frozen robot dot and highlighted room render as live with no badge or dimming: exactly the 'stale in the kitchen ghost' the live-pose feature was built to kill, reintroduced by the retention path and unmarked. survived.title: The storage-path mtime cache early-return omits the `map_id` check its sibling `_commit_result` performs, so map A's geometry is returned as map B's answer with `present: True`
survived.mechanism: `_refresh_storage_map_source` lines 257-266 reuses the cached result when `mtime` and `present_gate` match, and returns `cached['result']` directly. It never compares `cached.get('map_id')` to the `map_id` it was called with, and it never re-commits — so the cache entry keeps whatever map_id was stamped last. That is precisely the check `_commit_result` performs 140 lines earlier at line 117, annotated `# never serve another map's geometry`. The bypass is reachable because nothing in the Eufy source is map-scoped: `eufy_store_path` resolves ONE file per DEVICE (`.storage/robovac_mqtt.<serial>`) holding whatever map is current, and the presence gate `camera.{object_id}_map` (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:618) contains no {map_slug}, so `present` is identical across maps. The store lags by the fork's save-throttle — documented in this repo at adapters/eufy/adapter.py:645-648 ('The .storage robot position ... lags the fork's save-throttle'). So after a map switch the active-map select flips to B immediately while the store file is still map A with an UNCHANGED mtime: `mtime is not None and cached['mtime'] == mtime and cached['present_gate'] == present` all hold, and map A's rooms are returned as the answer for map B with `present: True` and no `stale` marker. Neither consumer can detect it: core/manager.py:4197 and sensor/map_overlays.py:52 both read `entry['result']` and never look at `entry['map_id']`.
survived.user_impact: For the window between a map switch and the fork's next store write, the card's room bboxes, the map-tap room resolution (`deviceRoomIdAtContentPct`) and the map_overlays sensor all describe the PREVIOUS floor's rooms while the backdrop shows the new one — a tap resolves to the old map's room number and dispatches a clean of the wrong room, with no error and no staleness indication. Narrower than LC-1: for Eufy this branch is only the fallback (`_refresh_eufy_map_source` is memory-primary and its `_mem_rooms_cache` is keyed by a content sha1, which IS correct), so it is reachable on installs whose fork exposes no in-memory `_map_data` (legacy builds, other forks, post-#136 attr drift) or during the startup window before the coordinator populates it.
survived.guards_checked: `_commit_result` line 117 — the sibling map_id guard that exists and is bypassed here. `present_gate` (line 263) — real, but map-independent for Eufy since the camera pattern has no {map_slug}, so it never differs between maps. `store_version` (line 269) guards the wrapper schema, not the map. `_compute_map_frame_gate` (core/manager.py:4275-4336) does NOT rescue this: it gates zone-draw/map-tap on the ROBOT re-localizing, its docstring explicitly assumes 'the raster + room list update immediately' (the exact assumption that fails here), and it is surfaced only through `_resolve_map_switcher`, which returns None when the fork's `*_map_select` entity is absent. Consumers core/manager.py:4197 and sensor/map_overlays.py:50-55 read the result with no map_id comparison.
confirmations: CONFIRMED. _refresh_storage_map_source:260-266 returns cached['result'] on mtime+present_gate match and never compares cached['map_id'] to the map_id argument, nor re-commits — bypassing the guard _commit_result:117 applies with the comment 'never serve another map's geometry'. The bypass is genuinely reachable: eufy_store_path resolves ONE file per DEVICE, and the Eufy live_map_image_entity_pattern is 'camera.{object_id}_map' (adapter.py:618) with no {map_slug}, so present_gate is identical across maps. survived.title: The same mtime early-return skips `_apply_inmem_pose_to_result`, freezing the robot/dock/current_room/path overlays for as long as the store file is unchanged
survived.mechanism: On a full read `_refresh_storage_map_source` calls `_apply_inmem_pose_to_result` at line 285 to make the fork's fresh in-memory pose AUTHORITATIVE over the moving fields (`apply_live_pose_override` clears stale current_room/path first). The mtime early-return at line 266 returns `cached['result']` and never calls it — so the moving overlays are served frozen at the timestamp of the last full parse. Because the store is save-throttled, an unchanged mtime is the COMMON case, not the rare one: the cache hit is the design goal ('an unchanged map costs one stat, not a 200 KB parse'), and it silently drags the pose along with the static segmentation. The memory branch demonstrates the correct pattern in the same file: `_refresh_eufy_map_source` caches only the STATIC scan (`_mem_rooms_cache`), shallow-copies it (line 440) and re-layers a fresh pose every call (line 441) — 'the pose changes every refresh; the static rooms scan does not'. The storage branch caches the whole result including the moving fields. `live_pose` and `memory` are independent adapter blocks, so an install where the fork exposes `_robot_pixel` but not `_map_data` gets the storage branch with a working live pose that is applied only on the rare ticks where the file changed.

survived.title: `_commit_result` is blind last-writer-wins across the storage path's two executor awaits — a refresh started before a map switch can commit after a newer one
survived.mechanism: Two independent triggers call `async_refresh_map_state_source` for the same vacuum with no serialization: the sensor platform's 60s timer (sensor/__init__.py:457) and EVERY dashboard-snapshot service call (services/snapshots.py:62). The memory-hit path is safe — `_refresh_eufy_map_source` contains no `await` between locating the MapData and `_commit_result`, so under HA's single event loop it is atomic. The storage path is not: `_refresh_storage_map_source` awaits `async_add_executor_job(_stat_mtime)` (line 251) and `async_add_executor_job(load_store_json)` (line 268), and `async_get_map_data_dict`/`async_get_map_render_data` await the same load. Across those gaps another refresh can complete end-to-end. `_commit_result`'s present branch (line 136) then overwrites unconditionally — there is no sequence number, generation token or per-vacuum lock, and the only map guard (line 117) sits on the ABSENT branch. So refresh#1 (map A, stat -> load -> slow) can commit AFTER refresh#2 (map B) finished, leaving the cache holding map A's result stamped map_id='A' while the active map is B.
survived.user_impact: Until the next tick (up to 60s, sooner if the card is polling), the snapshot and the map_overlays sensor serve the previous map's rooms/anchors under the new map — and since neither consumer compares `entry['map_id']` to the map they are rendering, nothing flags it. Self-correcting: the next stat sees the newer mtime, mismatches the committed one, and re-reads. Rated LOW because the window is one executor round-trip and the wrong state is transient, but it is a real gap ACROSS an await, not a synchronous-block false positive.

survived.title: Live-pose room lookup projects a MEMORY-frame robot pixel through STORAGE-frame geometry (no memory fallback, no store_version guard) — feeds room attribution at 2 s
survived.mechanism:
async_get_map_live_pose() reads the robot pixel from the fork's IN-MEMORY coordinator (_read_inmem_pose -> _robot_pixel, computed by the fork as (cur_pose - in-memory origin)/res) but resolves the geometry it normalizes against from _load_live_pose_geom(), which is .storage-ONLY (map_source_coordinator.py:476-498). Every other Eufy reader in this coordinator is memory-PRIMARY with a storage fallback (_refresh_eufy_map_source:397-435, async_get_map_data_dict:687-705, async_get_map_render_data:643-653); this one path is storage-only with no memory attempt. The pixel is then fed to current_room_for_pixel(map_data=STORAGE, px=MEMORY-frame) which subtracts the STORAGE ro_dx/ro_dy and indexes the STORAGE raster.

ARITHMETIC (real device numbers from .claude/notes/reference_eufy_intersession_coord_drift.md: origin=(-1367,-987), grid 360x300, res 5, outline origin +105 cells): stored map_data gives ro_dx = round((-842 - (-1367))/5) = 105. The device extends the map 1 m to the left; the fork's in-memory origin_x becomes -1467 while room_outline_origin_x stays -842, so the fork now computes px' = (pose + 1467)/5 = px + 20 and the correct offset is ro_dx' = round((-842 + 1467)/5) = 125, giving rx = px + 20 - 125 = rx_true. Using the LAGGED storage value the code computes rx = px + 20 - 105 = rx_true + 20 -> it reads the raster 20 cells = 20 x 5 cm = 1.00 m to the right of where the robot actually is, and returns the neighbouring room's id. 20 cells is far inside the raster, so the 0 <= rx < ro_w bound never fires.

survived.title: normalize_rendered CLAMPS out-of-grid pixels onto the map border instead of rejecting them, so off-grid raster cells and bad poses fold onto an edge rather than disappearing — diverging from the card's own decoder, which drops them
survived.mechanism:
normalize_rendered applies _clamp01 to both axes and always returns a valid pair; there is no way for a caller to distinguish 'this point is at the left edge' from 'this point is 25 cells off the map'. Three in-scope callers feed it unvalidated pixel coordinates:

(a) rooms_from_room_pixels (line 302-303) and zone_membership (line 387) map outline cell (rx, ry) to main grid (rx+ro_dx, ry+ro_dy) with NO bounds check against width/height. With the live device's ro_dx = 105 (origin -1367, outline origin -842, res 5) and an outline raster 300 cells wide, cell rx=280 lands at px=385 on a 360-wide grid: _clamp01(385/360) = _clamp01(1.0694) = 1.0. Every such cell collapses onto nx = 1.0. In zone_membership that means all of them pass the bbox reject for any zone drawn to the right edge (bx1 = 1.0) and are then counted in the >=90% dominance vote; in rooms_from_room_pixels the affected room's bbox is stretched to exactly 1.0.

(b) vacuum_to_normalized (line 217) projects hazard layers with px = (vx - origin_x)/res and no plausibility gate. The fork demonstrably carries TWO coordinate frames (map/biz frame spanning X[-1367,433] vs the raw DPS-179 telemetry frame at ~16000 — proven in reference_eufy_intersession_coord_drift.md). If a schema shift delivers the raw frame, px = (16000+1367)/5 = 3473 on a 360-wide grid -> _clamp01(9.65) = 1.0. hazards_from_mapdata then emits a valid-looking polygon squashed flat against the right edge, because _normalize_vacuum_point returns a truthy list and the `if p0 and p1` / `if len(pts) >= 3` tests (lines 511, 521) all pass.

(c) live_pose_overlay (line 582) pins an out-of-frame robot pixel to a map corner instead of omitting robot_anchor.

The card's own decoder does NOT do this: src/bindings/map.js:281-284 iterates px over [0, W) and `continue`s when rx/ry fall outside the raster, so out-of-grid cells are simply never drawn. Python folds them onto the border; JS drops them. The two decoders of the same raster disagree.

survived.title: correspondences_from_mapdata's docstring claims clamped corners are skipped; _mapdata_projector silently clamps with no detection, leaving the affine round-trip check as the only guard
survived.mechanism:
The docstring at line 534-535 states 'bad/clamped corners are simply skipped (the converter's round-trip check guards the rest)'. `proj` (lines 461-468) returns `[_clamp01(p.x / img_w), _clamp01(p.y / img_h)]` — it returns None only when the library transform RAISES. There is no clamp detection anywhere: a corner projecting outside the image silently becomes exactly 0.0 or 1.0 and is appended as a genuine correspondence at line 555, corrupting the least-squares fit that dispatch/zone_dispatch.py uses to place the drawn zone in device millimetres.

I proved this is NOT reachable under the shipped configuration and so it is latent, not live. homeassistant/components/roborock/__init__.py:94 builds MapParserConfig(map_scale=MAP_SCALE) with MAP_SCALE=4 (const.py:59) and no rotate and no trim, so vacuum_map_parser_base ImageConfig gives scale=4, rotation=0, trim=0. With those: ImageDimensions.to_img returns ((x/50 - L)*4, (H - (y/50 - T) - 1)*4) and the PIL image is (W*4, H*4). Room corners come from _image_to_map(room_px + image_left) (vacuum_map_parser_roborock/map_data_parser.py:244-247), so nx = room_img_x*4/(W*4) which is at most (W-1)/W < 1, and ny = (H - room_y - 1)*4/(H*4) which is at most (H-1)/H < 1. Both axes are strictly inside [0,1) — no clamp can fire. Non-zero rotation or trim would break that, and neither is reachable from HA today.

The surviving guard is max_residual_mm (zone_dispatch.py:85-99) at a 50 mm tolerance, computed over the SAME points that were fitted — a clamped outlier does perturb the fit enough to trip it, so the 'refuse rather than mis-dispatch' contract holds. The defect is the false docstring, not a live mis-dispatch.

Same `proj` is used by overlays_from_mapdata for user-drawn no-go areas, virtual walls and zones (lines 673-681), which CAN legitimately be authored beyond the trimmed map bounds; those clamp into distorted polygons on the overlay.
survived.user_impact: No live mis-dispatch today. The risk is that the docstring reads as an implemented safety guard, so a future change to the projector, the trim/rotate config, or the residual tolerance would remove the only real protection without anyone noticing the claimed one was never there. survived.title: A room's normalized bbox excludes its last pixel row/column while width_m/height_m on the same dict include it (+1) — the two size descriptors disagree by exactly one cell, and Roborock's equivalent omits the +1
survived.mechanism:
normalize_rendered returns the TOP-LEFT corner of a pixel's normalized band, so the bbox built at lines 302-304 spans [min_px/W, max_px/W] — the half-open extent, one column short of the room's real footprint. width_m at line 314 uses (max_px - min_px + 1) * res / 100 — the inclusive extent.

ARITHMETIC (live device grid W=360, res=5 cm): a room occupying main-grid columns 100..139 (40 cells). bbox x0 = 100/360 = 0.27778, x1 = 139/360 = 0.38611, span 0.10833. De-normalized with this module's own formula (zone_membership line 361: span * width * res / 100) that is 0.10833 * 360 * 5 / 100 = 1.950 m. width_m reports (139-100+1)*5/100 = 2.000 m. The two fields describe the same room and differ by exactly one cell (5 cm). For a 10-cell room (0.50 m) the bbox reports 0.45 m against width_m's 0.50 m — a 10% disagreement.

Cross-brand: rooms_from_mapdata (map_source_runtime.py:520) computes width_m = abs(x1-x0)/1000 from the parser's mm corners, which are themselves the exclusive extent (max_img_x - min_img_x) * 50 mm — NO +1. So the same physical geometry yields the inclusive metre value on Eufy and the exclusive one on Roborock.

survived.mechanism: find_mapdata(root, max_depth=6) is a bounded BFS whose predicate _is_mapdata (line 364) is `getattr(o,'image',None) is not None and getattr(o,'rooms',None) is not None`. The repo's own test model of the graph is flag-keyed: tests/unit/test_map_source_runtime.py:284 builds `_Coordinator(maps={0: md})`, i.e. `coordinator.maps` is a dict keyed by map flag holding one map per floor. BFS over a dict enumerates insertion order (map_source_runtime.py:256), so the FIRST map (flag 0) wins regardless of which map_id was asked for. The per-map image entity IS the correct root and is candidate 0 (roborock_candidates:1021-1023), but the image entity itself carries no MapData — the walk must descend through its `coordinator` attribute (not in _WALK_SKIP_ATTRS, line 224) into the SHARED coordinator, at which point the per-map scoping is gone. The second mechanism is the switch lag: `_home_trait._map_content.map_data` (the path recorded in .claude/notes/reference_map_source_lifecycle.md) holds only the CURRENTLY loaded map, refreshed on the roborock IMAGE_CACHE_INTERVAL (~30 s per docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md), while VA's active map_id flips as soon as `select.{id}_selected_map` changes — so for up to a refresh interval after a floor switch the walk returns the previous floor's MapData under the new map_id. The refuse-gate passes and `app_zoned_clean` is sent with millimetre coordinates computed in a different floor's frame.

survived.title: correspondences_from_mapdata's docstring claims clamped corners are skipped; the code feeds them into the least-squares fit, turning a rare edge case into an unexplained zone refusal
survived.mechanism: The docstring states 'bad/clamped corners are simply skipped (the converter's round-trip check guards the rest)' (:534-535). The code has no such guard: proj (map_source_runtime.py:461-468) returns `[_clamp01(p.x/img_w), _clamp01(p.y/img_h)]`, and _clamp01 (map_source.py:158-159) is `min(max(v,0.0),1.0)` — it returns a perfectly valid pair for an out-of-range input, so `if p:` at :553 is always true for a numeric projection and the clamped point is appended as if it were an exact correspondence. Since correspondences_from_mapdata feeds an unweighted least-squares fit (zone_dispatch.fit_normalized_to_mm:47-77), a clamped corner is an outlier that biases the whole affine, and max_residual_mm then measures the fit against that same corrupted point set. Arithmetic: a corner whose true normalized x is 1.004 on a 1024 px raster at 50 mm/px clamps to 1.0, a 0.004 x 1024 x 50 = 205 mm error — four times validate_tol_mm (50 mm), so normalized_rects_to_mm returns None and dispatch/manager.py:158-163 raises 'could not place the drawn zone on the device coordinate frame'. The safety outcome is correct (refuse, not mis-dispatch) — but the docstring's claimed mechanism does not exist, so the failure mode is a hard refusal instead of the documented graceful skip.

survived.title: Live pose is normalized and room-looked-up against .storage geometry while the map it is drawn on is memory-PRIMARY — the one reader never repointed
survived.mechanism: Every other Eufy reader in this subsystem was repointed to the fork's in-memory `_map_data` (P2 repoint): `_refresh_eufy_map_source` (L397-443) builds rooms from `mapdata_dict_from_obj(mem['obj'])` and then calls `_apply_inmem_pose_to_result(result, map_data=<that same in-memory dict>)`; `async_get_map_render_data` (L643-653) returns `render_data_from_storage(mem['map_data'])`; `async_get_map_data_dict` (L688-695) is memory-primary. `_load_live_pose_geom` (L476-498) is the sole survivor: it resolves `eufy_store_path` and returns `(store_json['data'])['map_data']` from the .storage FILE. `async_get_map_live_pose` (L520-527) then feeds that .storage map_data into `live_pose_overlay`, which uses it for BOTH `normalize_rendered(px,py,width,height)` and `current_room_for_pixel(map_data, px, py)` — while the robot pixel it is normalizing (`_robot_pixel`) was computed by the fork against the IN-MEMORY map's origin/res. The two map_data dicts are byte-identical in steady state (the P1 compare probe proved that), but they diverge whenever the in-memory map changes ahead of the fork's throttled store save: a re-segmentation or grid expansion changes width/height/origin_x/origin_y/room_outline_origin_*. This same device is documented to have gone from a room_outline offset of +105 cells (map_source.py:230 docstring) to 0 offset after a re-segmentation. Arithmetic with those two observed geometries and a live robot pixel (200,150) in the NEW frame: correct raster index rx=200-0=200; the .storage path computes rx=200-105=95 — a lookup 105 cells = 5.25 m to the left, returning a different room's id (or None). If the grid also resized (360x300 -> 420x340) the anchor moves too: nx=200/360=0.5556 served vs 200/420=0.4762 correct (8% of map width), ny=(300-1-150)/300=0.4967 vs (340-1-150)/340=0.5559 (6%). The live `path` (`normalize_trail`) rides the same dims. This is NOT display-only: listeners/pose_sampler.py:197 calls `async_get_map_live_pose` every ~2 s during a run and buffers `pose.get('current_room')` into `pose_samples`, which learning/external_ingest.py `_attribute` / `_apply_pose_identity` (L737, L768) consume to decide which rooms an external run cleaned and to stamp segment room identity.

survived.title: _norm_room_name normalises differently from slugify_room_name — it merges room identities that rooms/ keeps distinct, and lacks the NFC canonicalisation slugify was given specifically to prevent this
survived.mechanism: Two independent resolvers map the device's native current-room NAME to a room id. `listeners/pose_sampler.py:149-183` uses `slugify_room_name` (rooms/utils.py:11-44): strip, lower, drop `'` and `\"`, `&`->`and`, ` `->`_`, then Unicode NFC. The tracker uses `_norm_room_name` (tracker.py:47-49): strip, lower, then `re.sub(r'[\s_-]+', ' ', ...)`. Two concrete divergences. (a) SEPARATOR MERGE: rooms named "Guest-Room" and "Guest Room" slugify to "guest-room" and "guest_room" — distinct identities that rooms/ and the learning baselines key durable data on separately. `_norm_room_name` maps BOTH the slug and the name of BOTH rooms to the single string "guest room". `_detect_current_room` (tracker.py:417-424) iterates `rooms.items()` and returns the FIRST match, so whichever room happens to come first in dict order absorbs the attribution regardless of which room the device actually named. Note the direction: this is the tracker collapsing identities that rooms/ deliberately keeps apart, which is the opposite of the rooms/ slug-collision defect and is not fixed by fixing rooms/. (b) NO NFC: `slugify_room_name`'s docstring states the NFC step exists precisely because "a brand returning NFD on one firmware and NFC on another" would otherwise derive different keys for the same room. `_norm_room_name` does no Unicode canonicalisation, so a non-ASCII room name arriving decomposed (e.g. Cyrillic U+0418 + U+0306) while `room_data['name']`/`['slug']` are stored precomposed (U+0419) compares byte-unequal on both branches at tracker.py:421-422. pose_sampler matches it; the tracker returns None.
survived.user_impact: Case (a): live dwell is attributed to the wrong room id whenever two rooms' names differ only in a separator character, and the card's reanchored timeline marks the wrong room complete. Case (b): for non-ASCII room names in a decomposed form the tracker never matches, so `_detect_current_room` returns None every tick and — per TRK-3 — the entire run's dwell is credited to whatever room matched last, or nothing is ever attributed if none ever matched. The integration ships 18 language packs, so non-ASCII room names are an expected configuration. In both cases the tracker's answer disagrees with the pose sampler's answer for the same device signal, with no error surfaced.
survived.guards_checked: Read `slugify_room_name` (rooms/utils.py:11-44) in full and compared each transform step against `_norm_room_name` (tracker.py:47-49). Read `_resolve_managed_room_id` (listeners/pose_sampler.py:149-183) and confirmed it is the parallel resolver reading the SAME entity (`entities.active_cleaning_target`) via a different normalisation. Confirmed the tracker's two-branch compare at tracker.py:420-423 (slug OR name) IS a genuine rescue for the apostrophe and `&` cases — verified by hand: name "Kid's Room"/slug "kids_room" matches on the name branch, and "Kitchen and Dining" matches on the slug branch — so I am not reporting those. Confirmed `is_blank_state` (entity_helpers.py:28-41) short-circuits only the five blank sentinels and does not affect these cases. Confirmed `_detect_current_room` returns on first match with no ambiguity detection or tie-break.
confirmations: CONFIRMED by reading both normalizers. slugify_room_name (rooms/utils.py:34-44) does strip/lower, drops ' and ", maps & to 'and', maps space to '_', then NFC — it PRESERVES hyphens, so 'Guest-Room' -> 'guest-room' and 'Guest Room' -> 'guest_room' are distinct durable identities. _norm_room_name (tracker.py:47-49) collapses [\s_-]+ to a single space, mapping both slugs AND both names to 'guest room', and _detect_current_room (:417-425) returns the FIRST dict-order match with no ambiguity detection — so the tracker collapses identities rooms/ deliberately keeps apart. The NFC gap is also real: slugify's docstring states the step exists precisely to survive NFD/NFC firmware differences, _norm_room_name has no unicodedata call, and listeners/pose_sampler.py:167 resolves the SAME entity through slugify_room_name — so the two resolvers genuinely disagree on the same signal. The finder correctly declined to report the apostrophe/& cases, which the name-OR-slug two-branch compare does rescue.

CONFIRMED by reading both normalizers. slugify_room_name (rooms/utils.py:35-44): strip, lower, drop ' and ", &->and, space->_, then unicodedata.normalize('NFC'), with a docstring stating the NFC step exists exactly to stop a brand's NFD/NFC firmware difference deriving different keys. _norm_room_name (tracker.py:47-49): strip, lower, re.sub(r'[\s_-]+', ' ') — no NFC, and it collapses '-' and '_' and space to one character class, so 'Guest-Room' (slug guest-room) and 'Guest Room' (slug guest_room) both normalize to 'guest room' and _detect_current_room (417-425) returns the FIRST dict-order match with no ambiguity detection. Both divergences are real. Downgrading: each requires a specific room-naming configuration (two rooms differing only by separator, or a decomposed non-ASCII name stored precomposed), and the two-branch slug-OR-name compare genuinely rescues the apostrophe/& cases the finder correctly declined to report.

survived.title: Dock-drift append rewrites the entire log file on every reading, and a failed write silently forfeits that drift event via the already-committed _last_dock_pos
survived.mechanism: Two issues in the dock-drift path. (1) WRITE AMPLIFICATION: `_append_dock_drift` (tracker.py:173-223) is an append that is implemented as a full read-modify-write — `path.read_text().splitlines()` at line 198 loads the whole file, one record is appended, the list is roll-off trimmed to `DOCK_DRIFT_MAX_LINES = 5000`, then the ENTIRE list is re-serialised and rewritten via `tmp.write_text(...)` at line 218. Once the log saturates at 5001 lines (~90 bytes each, ~450 KB), every single logged reading costs a ~450 KB read plus a ~450 KB write and a rename. This is O(n) per append and O(n²) over the log's life, for a file described in its own comment as "Passive: append-only" — an append that never rewrites would be O(1). (2) LOST EVENT ON FAILURE: `_maybe_log_dock_drift` commits `self._last_dock_pos[vacuum_entity_id] = (vx, vy)` at tracker.py:165 BEFORE dispatching the write to the executor at line 168. If `_append_dock_drift` raises, the in-memory state already claims that position was logged, so the dedup at line 163 suppresses every subsequent identical reading and that drift event is never recoverable. The failure itself is not silent (`_LOGGER.exception` at line 221), but the data loss is unannounced and the `dx`/`dy` chain in the file becomes discontinuous — the next successful record's delta is computed against a position that was never written.
survived.user_impact: On an SD-card or eMMC HA install the rewrite amplification is real flash wear for a purely diagnostic log; the cost scales with how often the reported docked position jitters, which is exactly what the log exists to measure. Separately, the drift timeline the log is meant to provide can contain silent gaps and misleading dx/dy deltas after any transient write error, undermining its diagnostic purpose at the moment it matters.
survived.guards_checked: Confirmed the work runs off the event loop via `hass.async_add_executor_job` (tracker.py:168), so this is NOT blocking I/O on the loop — I am not claiming that. Confirmed `_dock_drift_lock` (tracker.py:135, held at line 184) correctly serialises concurrent executor appends within the instance, and that `tmp.write_text` + `tmp.replace(path)` (tracker.py:217-219) is a correct atomic-rename publish that cannot truncate the log on a crash — neither guard addresses the amplification or the pre-committed dedup state. Confirmed the roll-off logic at tracker.py:210-216 correctly preserves the `_meta` header line while trimming the body, so the cap itself works. Confirmed the dedup at tracker.py:162-164 and the docked/charging state gate at tracker.py:159-161 do bound the write rate to distinct positions only. Confirmed `except Exception` at line 220 uses `_LOGGER.exception`, so the failure is logged rather than swallowed.
confirmations: CONFIRMED, and correctly scoped. _append_dock_drift:196-219 is a full read_text().splitlines() -> append -> roll-off -> tmp.write_text -> replace on EVERY reading, i.e. O(n) per append against a 5000-line cap. The lost-event half is also real: _maybe_log_dock_drift commits self._last_dock_pos at :165 BEFORE dispatching the write at :168, so a raising _append_dock_drift leaves the dedup at :162-164 suppressing every subsequent identical reading and the next record's dx/dy computed against a position never written. The finder correctly does NOT claim loop-blocking (the work is on the executor) and correctly credits _dock_drift_lock and the atomic tmp+replace as real but orthogonal guards. LOW is right for a passive diagnostic log.

CONFIRMED both halves. _append_dock_drift (173-223) implements an append as a full read_text().splitlines() -> append -> roll-off -> tmp.write_text() -> replace, so at the 5000-line cap every logged reading costs a full read plus a full rewrite — O(n) per append for a file its own comment calls 'append-only'. And _maybe_log_dock_drift commits self._last_dock_pos[vid] = (vx, vy) at line 165 BEFORE dispatching the write at 168, so a write failure (logged at 221 but not compensated) leaves the dedup at 162-164 suppressing that reading forever and the next record's dx/dy computed against a position never written. The finder correctly declined to claim blocking-I/O (it is on the executor) and correctly credited the lock and the atomic tmp-rename. Diagnostic-only.

survived.title: start_job/end_job are dispatched to an executor thread on the strength of a comment describing disk I/O that start_job does not perform
survived.mechanism: listeners/lifecycle.py:226-237 wraps `tracker.start_job` in `hass.async_add_executor_job` justified by the comment "start_job is sync and performs disk I/O (`_load_samples_from_disk` / `_delete_samples_tmp_file`). Run it on the executor to avoid both the not-awaitable TypeError and the blocking-I/O warning." Neither method exists on `MappingTracker` — I read the class in full and grepped the file; there is no base class. `start_job` (tracker.py:286-310) does exactly three things: pop `_last_recorded_pos`, call `reset_job()`, and assign `_active_job[vac]`. Zero I/O. `end_job` (tracker.py:320-325) is likewise pure dict mutation and is dispatched the same way at listeners/lifecycle.py:339-344 with the comment "kept on the executor to stay off the loop." The comment describes behaviour the code does not have. The consequence is that `_active_job`, `_confidence` and `_last_recorded_pos` — dicts otherwise mutated exclusively from the event loop by the `@callback` `_handle_position_update` (tracker.py:368) — are written from an executor thread. `start_job` in particular calls `reset_job()` before assigning `_active_job`, so a position callback landing between those two statements sees a zeroed confidence state with no job and routes into the dock-drift branch instead of the confidence branch.
survived.user_impact: No user-visible failure proven: the individual dict operations are GIL-atomic and the interleaving window is a handful of bytecodes, so at worst one position sample is misrouted at job start. The real cost is that a false comment currently justifies threading loop-owned mutable state, which is the kind of claim a future change would build on — and it defeats the single-event-loop reasoning that makes the rest of this state machine analysable.
survived.guards_checked: Read `MappingTracker` in full (tracker.py:112-509) and confirmed no `_load_samples_from_disk` or `_delete_samples_tmp_file` member and no base class that could supply one. Read `start_job` (tracker.py:286-310) and `end_job` (tracker.py:320-325) statement by statement and confirmed neither touches the filesystem — the only file I/O in the module is `_append_dock_drift`, which is separately dispatched. Confirmed the 'not-awaitable TypeError' half of the comment is also moot: both are plain sync methods that could simply be called directly from the coroutine. Confirmed `_handle_position_update` is decorated `@callback` (tracker.py:368), i.e. it runs on the event loop, establishing the cross-thread contact. Confirmed no lock protects `_active_job` or `_confidence` (only `_dock_drift_lock` exists, and it covers the JSONL write alone).
confirmations: CONFIRMED. I read MappingTracker in full (tracker.py:112-509): there is no _load_samples_from_disk, no _delete_samples_tmp_file and no base class, so the justification comment at listeners/lifecycle.py:226-229 describes I/O that does not exist. start_job (:286-310) is three dict operations plus reset_job; end_job (:320-325) is pure dict mutation; the only filesystem work in the module is _append_dock_drift, dispatched separately. The consequence is accurate: both are dispatched via hass.async_add_executor_job, so _active_job/_confidence/_last_recorded_pos — otherwise mutated only from the @callback _handle_position_update on the loop (:368) — are written from an executor thread with no lock (only _dock_drift_lock exists, covering the JSONL write). The finder is appropriately honest that no user-visible failure is proven. LOW is right.

CONFIRMED. I read MappingTracker in full (tracker.py:112-509): there is no _load_samples_from_disk, no _delete_samples_tmp_file, and no base class — the justification comment at listeners/lifecycle.py:226-229 describes behaviour the code does not have. start_job (286-310) is three dict operations plus reset_job(); end_job (320-325) is pure dict mutation; the only file I/O in the module is _append_dock_drift, dispatched separately. The consequence — _active_job/_confidence/_last_recorded_pos written from an executor thread while _handle_position_update is a @callback on the loop (368), with no lock (only _dock_drift_lock exists, covering the JSONL write) — is real, and the finder was honest that the GIL makes the practical window a few bytecodes. The value is the false comment, not a demonstrated failure.

killed.title: current_room_for_pixel truncates toward zero with int() instead of flooring, so a slightly negative pixel resolves to grid cell 0 rather than being rejected as off-map
killed.mechanism:
Lines 418-419 do `rx = int(px) - ro_dx` / `ry = int(py) - ro_dy`. Python's int() truncates toward zero, so int(-0.4) = 0 and int(-0.9) = 0, whereas floor gives -1. For px in (-1, 0) the function therefore behaves as if the robot were at main-grid column 0 instead of one column off the grid.

ARITHMETIC: with ro_dx = 0 (the default when room_outline_origin_x is absent, since _outline_geometry line 243 defaults it to origin_x), px = -0.4 gives rx = 0, which passes the `0 <= rx < ro_w` bound at line 422 and returns whatever room id sits at raster cell 0 — a real room id for a pose that is off the map. Flooring would give rx = -1 and correctly return None. The asymmetry also means the truncation direction flips with sign: a pose at px = +0.4 rounds down to cell 0 (correct) while px = -0.4 rounds UP to cell 0 (wrong).

Separately, the anchor passed to normalize_rendered at line 582 of live_pose_overlay is NOT truncated, so the drawn robot dot and the resolved current_room can be derived from sub-pixel-different positions for the same anchor.
killed.user_impact: Narrow: requires a sub-pixel negative robot/trail coordinate, which the fork's integer _robot_pixel does not normally produce. When it does occur the robot is attributed to whichever room owns the raster's first cell instead of reporting 'not in a room', and that id flows into the same attribution stream as GEO-1.
killed.guards_checked: The `except (TypeError, ValueError)` around the conversion (line 420-421) catches non-numeric input only, not sign. The `0 <= rx < ro_w and 0 <= ry < ro_h` bound at line 422 is exactly what the truncation defeats, since it compares the already-truncated value. `idx >= len(raster)` (line 429) only catches a short raster. `0 < rid < _CATCH_ALL_RID` (line 432) filters background/catch-all ids but cell 0 commonly holds a real room. current_room_from_storage (line 443) passes trail[-1] through unvalidated beyond _numeric_pair.
killed_by: REFUTED — unreachable. int() vs floor only differs for a negative fractional px, and no caller can produce one. I grepped every caller of current_room_for_pixel: only map_source.py:443 (current_room_from_storage, trail[-1]) and :583 (live_pose_overlay, robot_pixel or dock_pixel). All of those originate in the fork's _pose_to_pixel (eufy-clean coordinator.py:541-550), which returns px=round(...) and RETURNS None unless 0<=px<width and 0<=py<height — so every pixel that ever reaches this function is a non-negative integer inside the grid. _dock_pixel is a previously captured _robot_pixel (coordinator.py:358-363) and _robot_trail entries are the same tuples; the .storage copies are those ints re-serialised (coordinator.py:993-995). For every reachable input int(px)==floor(px), and the sub-pixel-disagreement corollary is vacuous for integers. The finder itself concedes 'the fork's integer _robot_pixel does not normally produce' it — there is no path at all, not merely an unusual one.
confirmations: The code property is real: map_source.py:418-419 uses int() (truncation toward zero) so int(-0.4) == 0 passes the `0 <= rx < ro_w` bound at 422 and returns cell 0's room instead of None, and the sign asymmetry is genuine. But I found a rescue the finder did not: the fork's _pose_to_pixel (robovac_mqtt/coordinator.py:541-550) returns integers and returns None unless `0 <= px < width and 0 <= py < height`, so _robot_pixel and _robot_trail entries are never negative or fractional. The trigger is therefore essentially unreachable except as a corollary of GEO-1/POSE-1's frame mismatch. LOW confirmed and, if anything, generous.

Verified correct.

_MAP_SOURCE_HARD_CLEAR_REASONS coverage (lines 50-55) — I enumerated every absent `reason` this file and its callees can emit (not_configured, no_device, no_store, no_store_data, store_version_mismatch, live_map_absent, no_mapdata, no_segmentation, no_parsed_map, no_room_geometry, refresh_error, unknown_backend:<x>) and the structural/terminal ones are exactly the four in the set; `reason.startswith('unknown_backend')` correctly catches the formatted variant. Grid pixel px maps to image column px (band [px/W, (px+1)/W]); grid pixel py maps to image row H-1-py (band [(H-1-py)/H, (H-py)/H]).
